content: 1. Insert a single subdermal implant between days 1 and 5 of the menstrual cycle if there has been no hormonal contraceptive use in the past month. For detailed guidance on use following delivery, abortion, or miscarriage, refer to the manufacturer's package insert. The implant is effective for up to 3 years and must be replaced afterward. 2. The insertion procedure and technique vary between brands: Nexplanon: This implant is radiopaque, meaning it can be located using X-ray, CT, ultrasound, or MRI after insertion. Implanon: This implant is non-radiopaque and can only be located using ultrasound or MRI. 3. After removal of the implant, confirm that the entire device, which is 4 cm in length, has been extracted by measuring its length. If the implant is broken or bent while in place, the release rate of etonogestrel may slightly increase. It is crucial to remove the implant in its entirety. 4. Brigatinib reduces the levels or effectiveness of etonogestrel by inducing the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Brigatinib can also cause fetal harm, so women should use effective nonhormonal contraception during treatment and for at least 4 months after the last dose. 5. Carbamazepine decreases the levels or effectiveness of etonogestrel by inducing CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 6. Lesinurad decreases the effectiveness of etonogestrel by inducing CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Use additional nonhormonal contraceptive methods, as hormonal contraception alone is unreliable when taking lesinurad. 9. Lumacaftor/ivacaftor decreases the levels or effectiveness of etonogestrel through an unspecified mechanism. Avoid coadministration unless the benefits outweigh the risks. Hormonal contraceptives are not reliable during coadministration, and additional nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 10. Mavacamten decreases the levels or effectiveness of etonogestrel by inducing CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Progestin and ethinyl estradiol are CYP3A4 substrates, and mavacamten may reduce their systemic exposure, leading to contraceptive failure or breakthrough bleeding. Patients should use a contraceptive method unaffected by CYP450 induction (e.g., intrauterine system) or add nonhormonal contraception during coadministration and for 4 months after the last dose. 11. Omaveloxolone decreases the levels or effectiveness of etonogestrel by weakly inducing CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Hormonal contraceptives, including implants, may be less effective, so additional nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 12. Sugammadex sodium reduces the effectiveness of etonogestrel by receptor binding competition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. A sugammadex bolus dose is equivalent to missing doses of hormonal contraceptives. Patients must use additional nonhormonal contraception (e.g., condoms and spermicides) for 7 days after sugammadex administration. 15.
